hook: FOAM HOLED THE WING.|7 DIED 16 DAYS LATER.
photo_credit: Photo: NASA, Columbia's debris on the hangar grid (GPN-2003-00081) — Public domain

scenes.say: February 2003. Space Shuttle Columbia breaks apart over Texas, sixteen minutes from landing.

At launch, foam from the fuel tank hit the left wing and holed panel 8 of its heat shield. Sixteen days later, on the way home, superheated air got in through that hole and melted the wing from the inside.

The tank was required to shed no debris. The panels were built for an impact of zero point zero zero six foot-pounds. But foam had come off on earlier flights, and it was treated as normal. Same wing. One hole.
Investigators recovered eighty-four thousand pieces of Columbia. All seven astronauts aboard were killed.

comment: Foam had hit the shuttle on earlier flights and was accepted as normal. Would you have grounded the fleet? The full step-by-step breakdown is on the channel.
